clue.text: Unclear how unfortunate cubs got covered in mineral

indicators.note: something unfortunate has had things go wrong, so the letters fall out of their proper order
to be covered in something is to sit wrapped inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: ore is rock from which a mineral or metal is extracted
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer wonders how some hapless bear cubs ended up caked in mineral dust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got covered in' reads as the cubs getting dirty, but it tells you the jumbled cubs go inside the mineral, the crossword's favourite three-letter one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure is hard to make out or understand, a close synonym for vague or murky.

clue.text: The reason inquisitive children get eventually

definitions.text: The reason inquisitive children get eventually

blocks.clueFragment: The reason inquisitive children get eventually
blocks.note: surface reading: a remark about how curious children finally learn why things happen
setter's reading: the word a weary parent finally answers after a long chain of 'why?' questions

explanation.walkthrough: Children who keep asking 'why?' are eventually fobbed off with the one-word reply that is no explanation at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The word introduces a reason in ordinary speech, and is the stock exhausted reply parents give to endless questioning.

clue.text: Company boss integrates R&D as an article of faith

indicators.note: to integrate is to absorb parts into a whole, so letters are taken inside another word

blocks.note: chief executive officer, the head of a company
the two letters R and D, taken as printed

explanation.surface: A chief executive brings research and development into the core of the company's beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: The R and the D are slotted separately into CEO: C + R + E + D + O.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of belief, literally Latin for 'I believe', so a principle someone holds firmly.

clue.text: Tell the story of disputed election result

blocks.note: first meaning: to narrate events
second meaning: a second tally of votes demanded after a close or contested poll

explanation.surface: Someone narrates the saga of a contested vote.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb (stress on the second syllable) and the noun (stress on the first) are spelt alike.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means narrate; as a noun it is a fresh counting of ballots after a challenged poll.

clue.text: It's much taller, said Spooner, getting confused

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so his version of a phrase trades its initial sounds

blocks.note: 'way higher' means much taller; swap the W and H sounds

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a building's height but muddles their words.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of 'way higher' gives 'hay wire'; 'getting confused' also nods at Spooner's own slips.
explanation.definitionFit: To go haywire is to go wrong or become muddled, from tangled baling wire on farms.

clue.text: Agents dropping fine group of players

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun; the definition names the players collectively

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so a letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: a factor is an agent who acts on someone else's behalf
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Talent agents cut a good band from their books.
explanation.walkthrough: FACTORS loses its F. 'Players' here are performers on stage, not sports players or musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Players is an old word for stage performers, so a company of players is a cast of performers.

clue.text: Liberal Party wet a renowned law enforcer?

indicators.note: liberal can mean loose or free, not strictly bound, so the letters are freely rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician from the Liberal Party is a feeble, wet sort of enforcer of the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal Party' reads as the British political party, but Liberal is the signal. In British politics 'wet' means feeble or moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyatt Earp was the famous Wild West lawman of Tombstone, Arizona, known for the gunfight at the O.K. Corral.

clue.text: Right old passion for country

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
O is a common abbreviation for old
a mania is an intense enthusiasm or craze

explanation.surface: Someone's old patriotic fervour for their homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: Three pieces in a row: R + O + MANIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a nation in south-eastern Europe, so it is simply one example of a country.

clue.text: Disorganised NHS lab flooded with body parts

definitions.note: the answer is the substance of the body rather than separate parts

indicators.note: disorganised things are in disarray, so the letters lose their order and are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; the NHS is Britain's National Health Service
taken as written, joining the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A chaotic National Health Service laboratory is swamped with body parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flooded with' reads as a container, but 'flooded' is itself fodder and 'with' simply joins it to NHS LAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Flesh and blood is the physical substance of a living body, the material its parts are made of.

clue.text: Top class haven for millions — it can't be bettered

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a noun meaning the peak

indicators.note: a haven shelters whatever comes to it, so one word gives refuge to a letter inside it

blocks.note: ace means first-rate, excellent
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A luxurious tax haven for millionaires is the best there is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haven for millions' suggests a tax haven, but it means ACE shelters M.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point or perfection of something, the peak beyond which nothing is better.

clue.text: Small actor excited by order to fight

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters get jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A minor performer gets worked up when told to start a fight scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The two opening words supply all ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A call to arms is a summons to take up weapons, a command for troops to go into battle.

clue.text: University gets kudos, having cracked this puzzle

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so the letters are smashed and reassembled

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A university earns praise after solving a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked this puzzle' reads as solving it; 'cracked' is really the anagram signal and 'this puzzle' the definition, though a crossword is not one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudoku is the popular Japanese number-placement grid puzzle, so it is a fair example of a puzzle.

clue.text: Inspection finds minuscule attachment to fastener, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a screw is a fastener, and the minuscule (tiny) word is attached after it

explanation.surface: An inspector spots a tiny part fixed to a bolt or screw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attachment to' says the small word is tacked on after the fastener; together they are said 'screw tiny'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutiny is close, careful examination, so it is a direct synonym of a thorough inspection.

clue.text: Food colonists found initially inside wood

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is used
inside means within, so a letter sits enclosed by another word

blocks.note: bees live in colonies
the opening letter of found
teak is a hardwood

explanation.surface: Settlers discover something to eat deep in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colonists' suggests settlers, but here they are insects that live in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefsteak is a thick slice of beef for grilling, so it is one specific example of food.

clue.text: Quite large digit can cause input error

blocks.note: fat means plump or sizeable
a finger is a digit of the hand

explanation.surface: A chunky finger can hit the wrong key while typing.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue nearly describes the error itself, and the phrase is named after exactly that clumsy fingertip.
explanation.definitionFit: A fat-finger mistake is a typing slip where a key next to the intended one gets pressed, especially costly in trading.

clue.text: Pedestrian being initially very fussy

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so just the first letter of the word is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of being
anal is informal for obsessively fussy or perfectionist

explanation.surface: A person on foot is being finicky from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' looks like a noun for a walker; it is the adjective meaning dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means dull and unimaginative, which is just what trite or commonplace work is.

clue.text: Plain clothes include a couple of accessories lacking finish

indicators.note: to lack a finish is to have no ending, so the last letter of each word is removed

blocks.note: two accessories: a muff for warming the hands and a tie

explanation.surface: A casual outfit still includes a couple of accessories, unfinished ones.
explanation.walkthrough: Each accessory loses its last letter: MUF(F) + TI(E). A muff is a fur tube for warming the hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Mufti is ordinary civilian dress worn by someone who normally wears a uniform, especially a soldier or police officer.

clue.text: Open and happy face

blocks.note: feeling up means cheerful
the face of a building is its front

explanation.surface: A description of someone with a frank, cheerful expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' must be read as candid rather than unlocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Being upfront means being honest and frank, hiding nothing, which is what an open person is.

clue.text: Singer paid thief, when compromised

indicators.note: something compromised has been damaged or corrupted, so the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A vocalist pays off a burglar once their security has been breached.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words between the definition and the signal supply all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Piaf was the celebrated French chanteuse famous for 'La Vie en rose', so she is a singer.

clue.text: Willing to put everything one has under tension

indicators.note: in a down answer, being under something means being written below it, so this piece comes second

blocks.note: T is the symbol for tension in physics
a person's estate is all the property they own

explanation.surface: Someone is prepared to stake all they own in a tense moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' looks like eager, but it means making a will; fittingly, the estate is what the will disposes of.
explanation.definitionFit: Testate describes someone who died having made a valid will, so it means will-making in the legal sense.

clue.text: Regularly pass up rest to get the black stuff

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
a halt is a stop or rest

explanation.surface: Someone keeps skipping a break to collect the dark material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass up' reads as decline, but it is simply the source of letters. 'The black stuff' can also suggest Guinness.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the dark tarry material used to surface roads, so it is literally black stuff.

clue.text: Constant pessimist has no yen for alfresco dining

indicators.note: having none of something means it is missing, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: pi is the mathematical constant
a cynic expects the worst
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A habitual pessimist has no appetite for eating outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' reads as a craving, but it is the currency, giving one letter to remove: PI + C(Y)NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is a meal eaten outdoors, and alfresco means in the open air.

clue.text: Approved adding spicier centre in cheapest meat

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the middle letters are kept
in means placed within, so these letters go inside another word

blocks.note: offal is the organ meat, traditionally the cheapest cuts
the middle three letters of spicier

explanation.surface: A cook is authorised to add a hotter core to the cheapest meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approved' could be the past tense of a verb, but it is the adjective; offal (organ meat such as liver and kidneys) is traditionally the cheapest cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Official means authorised or sanctioned by those in charge, which matches approved.

clue.text: Careless agent retaining cut

indicators.note: to retain something is to keep hold of it, so one word holds another inside

blocks.note: a spy is a secret agent
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A negligent agent hangs on to a percentage of the takings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as a share of money, but it is the verb to chop: S(LOP)PY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy work is slapdash and lacking care, a direct synonym of careless.

clue.text: When to act? As soon as union gets involved

indicators.note: involve originally means to wrap up or envelop, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: 'once' can mean as soon as, as in 'once you arrive'
U is the abbreviation for union

explanation.surface: A question about when to take industrial action, answered: as soon as the trade union joins in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act' points to strikes, but it means perform on stage, where an actor comes in at the agreed signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor speaks or moves on cue, at the prompt signal, so the phrase names the moment to perform.

clue.text: French author going after ugly woman for cheese

indicators.note: going after means following behind, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: a gorgon is a hideous woman, after the snake-haired monsters of Greek myth
Émile Zola was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A French writer pursues a plain woman in search of cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The author comes first in the clue but last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgonzola is a blue-veined Italian cheese named after a town near Milan.

clue.text: Colour of extremely comfy afghan

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the two ends, so only the outer letters of each word are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of comfy
the first and last letters of afghan

explanation.surface: A question about the shade of a very cosy knitted blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: An afghan is a knitted or crocheted blanket; 'extremely' serves both words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is a greenish-blue hue, one of the printing primaries, so it is a kind of colour.

clue.text: Pull back piece of dustcart taillight

indicators.note: a piece of something is a portion of it, so the letters sit within the words
going back means moving the other way, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone salvages part of a bin lorry's rear light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull back' reads as retreat, but 'back' belongs to the wordplay. A dustcart is a British rubbish truck.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to draw something towards you, as a magnet does, which is a sense of pull.

clue.text: Theatre worries, showing cheap TV programmes?

blocks.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
'what's eating you?' means what is worrying you

explanation.surface: Theatre people fret that television is filled with low-budget shows.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that repeats are cheap because they were already paid for.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters rerun old shows because they cost far less than commissioning new ones, hence a cheap schedule filler.
